name: Garmin
description: Garmin designs and manufactures GPS-based and sensor-based devices and sells them in five lines: Fitness wearables and cycling devices (32 percent of FY2025 sales), Outdoor adventure watches and handhelds (28 percent), Marine chartplotters and autopilots (16 percent), Aviation avionics (14 percent) and Auto OEM domain controllers and infotainment sold to carmakers (9 percent, loss-making). It is vertically integrated, making most products in its own factories (Taiwan, US, Poland), so its margin is a hardware margin rather than a retailer's. FY2025 net sales were about $7.25 billion (computed sum of segments) and operating income about $1.88 billion, with Fitness and Outdoor producing about three quarters of profit.

hq.note: Swiss-incorporated; principal operations in Olathe, Kansas, USA (FY2025 10-K properties)

employees.note: About 23,000 full and part-time: 8,100 Americas, 11,400 APAC, 3,500 EMEA (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Fitness
businessLines.how: Consumers pay a one-time price for a watch or bike device (often $200 to $1,000), sold through retailers and online; some subscription services on top. Growth is driven by wearables upgrades.
businessLines.description: Wearables, cycling products and health and wellness devices for consumers

operatingProfit.note: Computed: segment gross profit minus segment operating expenses from the 10-K segment table

businessLines.name: Outdoor
businessLines.how: One-time device sales through retail and online; adventure watches drove FY2025 growth.
businessLines.description: Adventure watches, golf devices, dog tracking and handheld GPS

operatingProfit.note: Computed: segment gross profit minus segment operating expenses from the 10-K segment table

businessLines.name: Aviation
businessLines.how: Sold to airframe manufacturers (OEM) for installation in new aircraft and to owners as aftermarket retrofits; high-price, certified products with long design cycles.
businessLines.description: Panel avionics, autopilot and portable aviation products for aircraft makers and the aftermarket

operatingProfit.note: Computed: segment gross profit minus segment operating expenses from the 10-K segment table

businessLines.name: Marine
businessLines.how: Sold to boat builders (OEM) and to boaters through dealers and retail; chartplotters led FY2025 growth.
businessLines.description: Chartplotters, sonar, autopilots and audio for boats

operatingProfit.note: Computed: segment gross profit minus segment operating expenses from the 10-K segment table

businessLines.name: Auto OEM
businessLines.how: Contracted supply to carmakers per vehicle programme; low gross margin (16.7 percent) and a segment operating loss in FY2025.
businessLines.description: Domain controllers and infotainment systems supplied to vehicle manufacturers

operatingProfit.note: Computed: segment gross profit minus segment operating expenses from the 10-K segment table
